title.en: Ground rules prior to starting emr training

statement.en: ESGE recommends that, prior to starting training and the establishment of a trainee–trainer relationship, the ground rules listed below should be established.

text.en: Endoscopists who provide training in EMR (EMR trainers) should have fulfilled the requirements in this competency framework (Recommendation 37), be aware of their own outcomes, and follow them up (Recommendation 38).

Trainees in EMR should first undertake a period of observation: watching experts perform procedures and verbalizing thoughts on lesions and the approach to their resection. The number of procedures is not specified and should be agreed during discussion between the trainee and the trainer.
During this observation period, the relevant literature on endoscopic resection should be thoroughly reviewed (including the content of Recommendations 3–7).
Training in EMR to become competent (as defined in this curriculum) is best accomplished during a dedicated fellowship of >6 months.

During any fellowship, trainees should not initially expect to fully complete all cases (establishing ground rules is critical). Recommendation 28 may form a structure for discussing the ground rules of training.
The SMSA and SMSA+ scores may be helpful to guide which lesions are suitable for initial training ([Table 2]) [36].

Training should be competency based, rather than based on specific numbers of procedures, perhaps focusing on a particular skill per lesion; for example, lesion assessment, injection technique, snare selection, and placement technique etc. in the manner outlined in the following sections.

Training should commence on lesions of <30 mm in standard colonic locations (not those described in the SMSA+ score) and progress to larger lesions, difficult locations/difficult access etc. as skills develop.
EMR trainers should ideally have attended a course on the theory of training and how it applies to training in endoscopy (train-the-trainers course).
